title: ದಾಸನಾದೆನೋ ಹರಿ ದಾಸನಾದೆ
charanas:
ಅಸುರಕುಲದಿ ಜನಿಸಿ ಅಸುರಾರಿಯ ಪಾದ ಭಜಿಸಿದ
ಅಸೂಯೆಕೋಪದಿ ಹಿರಣ್ಯಕ ಹಸುಗೂಸನು ಕೊಲಬಯಸಿದ
ಬಿಸುಟನು ಗಜ ಸರ್ಪ ಗಿರಿ ಸಾಗರ (ವಿಷ) ಬೆಂಕಿಗ್ಹೂಡಿದ ನರ
ಸಿಂಹ ಬಂದ ಕಂಬದಿಂದ ಪ್ರಹ್ಲಾದನ ಮೊರೆ ಕೇಳಿ

ಭುವಿಗಿಳಿದರು ಪ್ರಹ್ಲಾದ ಮುನಿವರೇಣ್ಯ ಶ್ರೀವ್ಯಾಸ ತೀರ್ಥ
ಭುವಿಪತಿಯ ಕುಹುಯೋಗವ ಗುರುರಾಜನಾಗಿ ಹರಿಸಿದ
ಸವಿಯುತ ಶ್ರೀಕೃಷ್ಣಾಂಕಿತರು ವ್ಯಾಸತ್ರಯವ ರಚಿಸಿದ
ರವಿಯಂತೆ ಸಲಹಿದ ವಾದಿರಾಜ ಕನಕ ಪುರಂದರಗೆ

ವಿದ್ಯಾನಿಧಿ ಸುಧೀಂದ್ರ ಶಿಷ್ಯ ಪ್ರಹ್ಲಾದರೇ ಪರಿಮಳಾಚಾರ್ಯ
ವೈದ್ಯರು ಭವರೋಗ ಕಳೆವ ಮಂತ್ರಾಲಯದಿ ನೆಲೆಸಿಹ ವೇದ-
-ವೇದ್ಯ ಮೂಲ ರಾಮರ ಭಕ್ತಿಯ ಸೂಸಿ ಹಾಡಿದ ಗುರುರಾಯ
ವಂದ್ಯರು ಜಗನ್ನಾಥ ಗೋಪಾಲ ವಿಜಯ ಮುಕುಂದ ವಿಠಲ ದಾಸರ

pallavi.en: I have become a servant, O, a servant of Hari.

anupallavi.en: I am a servant at the feet of those who spread far and wide the divine plays (līlās) of the lotus feet of the Thousand-Named Lord.

charanas.en:
Born into the clan of the asuras, he worshipped the feet of Hari, the foe of the asuras. In envious, boundless rage, Hiraṇyaka set out to kill his tender child. He flung him before elephants and serpents, off the mountain and into the sea, and gave him to poison and fire. Then Nara-siṃha burst from the pillar, hearing Prahlāda's plea.
Sung into the refrain, the line goes on: hearing Prahlāda's plea, the plea of a boy who urged even his fellow asura children to chant Hari's name, I became a servant, a servant of Hari. The word kēḷi also means "divine sport", so it echoes the līlās of the anupallavi.

Prahlāda himself descended to earth as the foremost of sages, Śrī Vyāsa Tīrtha. When the inauspicious Kuhu-yoga hung over the king, he took the throne himself as guru-king and turned the danger away. Sweetly, under the signature "Śrī Kṛṣṇa," he composed the Vyāsatraya (Nyāyāmṛta, Tarkatāṇḍava, Tātparya Candrikā), his three great treatises. Like the sun, he nurtured Vādirāja, Kanaka and Purandara.
Sung into the refrain, the last line goes on: to Vādirāja, Kanaka and Purandara, the disciples warmed and raised by that sun, I became a servant, a servant of Hari.

He is the treasury of learning, disciple of Sudhīndra, Prahlāda himself, the Parimaḷācārya who gave us the Parimaḷa. He is the physician who cures the sickness of worldly existence, and he dwells at Mantrālaya. He poured out his devotion in song to Mūla Rāma, the Lord known through the Vedas. He is Guru Rāya, worthy of the homage of the dāsas Jagannātha, Vijaya and Gopāla, and of all the servants of Lord Mukunda Viṭṭhala.
Sung into the refrain, the last line goes on: I became the servant of the servants of Mukunda Viṭṭhala, a servant of Hari.

notes: In praise of the avatara traya - Bhaktharaja Prahlada, Shri Vyasathirtha, Shri Raghavendra thirtha.
